div.head: I Ew 1.5
div.ab: Eac we cwædon: gif enig yfelra manna wære ðe wolde oðres yrfe to borge settan for wiðertihtlan, ðæt he gecyþe ðonne mid aðe, ðæt he hit for nanum facne ne dyde, ac mid fulryhte butan brede ⁊ bigswice; ⁊ se dyde þonne swa ðer he dorste, ðe hit man ætfenge: swa he hit agnode swa he hit tymde.

Eac we cwædan: gif hwa gemearra manna wære ðe wolde oðres yrfe to borge seatan for wiðertihtlan, þæt he gecyðe ðonne mid aðe, þæt he hit for nanum facne ne dyde, ac mid folcrihte butan bræde ⁊ biswice; ⁊ se dyde ðonne swa ðer he dorste, ðe hit man ætfence: swa he hit ahnode swa he hit tymæde.

Etiam diximus: si aliquis malorum esset, qui uellet alterius pecus per plegium mittere pro ƿiðertihlan (id est pro iniusta accusatione), ut hoc iureiurando monstret, quod pro nullo facinore faciat, sed plena rectitudine butan brede ⁊ bigsƿice (id est sine figmento et seductione); et faciat quod audeat super quem inuenitur: uel sibi propriet uel aduocet.

Eac we cwædon; gif enig yfelra manna wære ðe wolde oðres yrfe to borge settan for wiðertihtlan, ðæt he gecyþe ðonne mid aðe, ðæt he hit for nanum facne ne dyde, ac mid [folcrihte] butan brede ⁊ bigswice; ⁊ se dyde þonne swa ðer he dorste, ðe hit man ætfenge: swa he hit agnode, swa he hit tymde.

Auch bestimmten wir — [gegen den Fall] wenn es da einen der bösen (betrügerischen B) Menschen giebt, der kraft widerrechtlicher Klage jemandes Vieh unter Pfand[sicherheit] bringen will —, dass der [Anefänger zuerst] dann erkläre unter Eid, ‘dass er dies zu keinerlei Truge thut, sondern nach Volksrecht (vollem Recht H) ohne List und Tücke’; und der [Verklagte], bei welchem jenes im Anefang angegriffen wurde, handele alsdann so, wie er sich da getraut: entweder er erkläre es als sein eigen, oder er ziehe es zur Gewähr.

We also determined — [against the case] where there is one of the evil (deceitful B) men who wishes to put someone’s livestock under pledge by virtue of an unlawful claim — that the [attacher first] then declare on oath ‘that he does this for no fraud, but according to folk-law (full right H) without trickery or deceit’; and let the [accused], from whom it was attached, then act as he dares: either let him declare it his own, or let him vouch it to warranty.

We have further declared, that, if there is any evil man who by way of a countercharge wishes to place another’s livestock under distraint, he shall swear an oath that he does it for no wicked end, but in accordance with public law and without fraud and guile; and in that case he in whose possession the stock has been attached, shall adopt whichever he dares to [of the following two courses]: either he shall substantiate his title to it, or he shall vouch it to warranty.

Laut jener Formel scheint fullan folcrihte richtige Lesung, die sowohl H wie Q flüchtig zusammenzogen. Oder aber B wusste die Formel auswendig und besserte danach. Folcriht liest auch II As 10, wo dieselbe Formel angezogen wird. — Die Worte ‘ohne List und Tücke’ braucht Urk. Bi 486

According to that formula fullan folcrihte seems the correct reading, which both H and Q carelessly contracted. Or else B knew the formula by heart and corrected accordingly. II As 10, where the same formula is cited, also reads Folcriht. — The words ‘without guile and deceit’ are used in the charter Bi 486

Quadr. adds an explanatory parenthesis after wiðertihtlan: ‘id est pro iniusta accusatione.’ Liebermann following Quadr. translates ‘kraft widerrechtlicher Klage.’ Thorpe explains it as ‘a cross action resorted to for purposes of delay and oppression’; it was forbidden by II Can. cap. 27.
The form of the oath, Liebermann suggests, may be that given in The Formulæ for Oaths, cap. 2.
